findingDetails.title: acceptance-criteria.md states two incompatible completion states and miscounts its own rows
findingDetails.evidence: Status Complete at :44 and Closeable No at :98 while AC-017 is Unmet at :73; the continuity block still says next_safe_action None; the packet is complete (:17) with completion_pct 100 (:24), last updated 2026-10-01. The closure sentence at :100 claims 16 active criteria are Met while its own next sentence says AC-017 stays Unmet; grep counts 15 Met, 1 Unmet, 1 Superseded rows. tasks.md:138 (CHK-020, P0) is checked with evidence claiming 16 Met rows. spec.md:37 says In Progress.
findingDetails.recommendation: Reconcile closure metadata: keep In Progress with completion_pct reflecting AC-017 Unmet and next_safe_action push and confirm the CI run; correct the closure sentence and CHK-020 evidence to 15 Met, 1 Superseded, 1 Unmet; align spec.md with acceptance-criteria.md.

findingDetails.title: the same replay evidence is pinned to two different commit ranges
findingDetails.evidence: AC-013 and implementation-summary.md:153 cite 38b2135472^..03afeb4552; spec.md:302 and tasks.md:276 (T030) cite f8519088b9..03afeb4552. git log shows 6 commits vs 23 commits; the second range is a superset covering f8519088b9 and 16 earlier commits. All three deviation SHAs (4ceef9d5e7, 4754d270ab, 7488e80836) sit in both ranges, so at most one citation matches the run whose transcript produced the flags-exactly-three result.
findingDetails.recommendation: Pin one range everywhere (the missed range f8519088b9..03afeb4552 named by the investigation and T030), or re-run and record the actual range in every citation.
findingDetails.downgradeTrigger: withdrawn if a recorded transcript shows both ranges produced identical output

findingDetails.title: no playbook scenario exercises the three new rule ids
findingDetails.evidence: GIT-045 exercises --explain resolution, subject.format, body.required, bypass removal and an edited maxLength to subject.max-length (:29-33, :49). rg over the playbook tree finds no subject.scope-alias, subject.length-target or body.breaking-sections, so the three rules the follow-up adds have unit and hook coverage but no operator scenario, while T024 audited the playbook for the contract surface.
findingDetails.recommendation: Extend GIT-045 or add one scenario covering an alias scope, an 81-character subject warning and a missing breaking section; the follow-up scope excluded the playbook, so schedule the coverage or record the deferral explicitly.

findingDetails.title: the 80/100 limits are restated as literals in prose surfaces no drift check covers
findingDetails.evidence: warnLength 80 / maxLength 100 in the rules block (:238-239) also appear as literals in template prose (:35) and self-check bullets (:162-163) and in SKILL.md:341. templateDriftErrors (message-contract.mjs:664-681, matcher :676) compares only backticked rule ids and never passes SKILL.md; a limit edit updates the JSON, keeps tests green, and leaves both prose surfaces teaching the old numbers.
findingDetails.recommendation: Make the drift guard value-aware or make the prose reference the keys symbolically as the section 7 rule table does; extend the check to SKILL.md wording it must keep in sync.

results.detail: REQ-013 to alias rule (message-contract.mjs:435-437, shape :186-192, rule id :345; template :227-232); REQ-014 to warn rule (:462-464, :351; template warnLength :239); REQ-015 to sections rule (:537-548, :356; template :253); REQ-016 to corrected example (template :132) and SKILL.md :341, :385-387; REQ-017 to unit tests, hook case commit-msg.test.sh:415-447 and CI step workflow :41-42.

Evidence rows cite real lines, but R3-P2-001 and R3-P2-002 are evidence-accuracy defects in the closure chain; suite pass counts (24/24, PASS=31) were not executed under containment and remain INFERRED.

No agent-gate file is in the diff; the gate imports validateCommit from the shared library (iteration 2 verified git-message-gate.mjs:31, call :331), so the new rules reach the agent surface without gate edits.
Hermes mirror regenerated with identical wording (diff of .hermes/skills/sk-git/SKILL.md); .opencode/.pi/.claude skill dirs are symlinks to ../.skilled/skills, so the canonical edit propagates.

message-contract-enforcement.md still matches the code (resolution order :29, gate table :35-40) and defers rule enumeration to the template block (:19); no catalog claim invalidated by the three new keys.
GIT-045 covers the block editability and the older rules but none of the three new rule ids; reported as R3-P2-003.
